info.name: Snowflake Code Bundle Executions API
info.description:
The Snowflake Code Bundle Executions API is a REST API that you can use to execute a code bundle directly from a stage location, without first creating a named code bundle, and to monitor or cancel those executions. An execution started this way has no named code bundle backing it and does not live under a specific database or schema, so this resource is exposed at the account level.

Contact Support:
 Name: Snowflake, Inc.
 Email: support@snowflake.com

query.description: Filter by code bundle name. To match a case-sensitive or special-character identifier, wrap the value in double quotes (for example "0303_replace_test"). Combine with database and schema to scope to a fully qualified bundle.
Filter by the database supplied when the code bundle was created or executed.
Filter by the schema supplied when the code bundle was created or executed.
Exact match on the executed entrypoint file path.
Inclusive lower bound on the execution start time, interpreted as TIMESTAMP_LTZ. Accepts any timestamp literal (for example 2026-07-07 or 2026-07-07T00:00:00).
Inclusive upper bound on the execution start time, interpreted as TIMESTAMP_LTZ.
Comma-separated, case-insensitive list of bundle types to include. Allowed values: custom, ml, spark.
Comma-separated, case-insensitive list of compute types to include. Allowed values: warehouse, compute_pool, serverless.
Comma-separated, case-insensitive list of language types to include. Allowed values: python, java, scala.
Filter by a single execution status (case-insensitive). Allowed values: pending, running, done (succeeded), failed, cancelled (canceled), deleted.
Exact match on the caller-supplied execution name.
Query id of the execute-code-bundle statement, to scope history to a single execution.
Maximum number of rows to return. Clamped to [1, CODE_BUNDLE_HISTORY_MAX_RESULT_LIMIT] (default 100).

request.description: List code bundle executions in the account, optionally filtered by bundle, entrypoint, time range, type, status, execution name, or query id. All query parameters are optional; with none supplied, recent executions are returned (up to the result limit).

response.name: successful
